title: What a ZPA Private Service Edge is
aliases: private service edge for private access
is the zpa pse the same as the zia pse
pse vs public service edge zpa

prose.text: A ZPA Private Service Edge (PSE) is the customer-side session broker of Private Access; Internet & SaaS has its own Service Edges.

prose.label: Identity.
prose.text: {{single-tenant-broker}} {{broker-function}} {{zpa-appliance}} The appliance is described in [[zpa.software-components.appliance]], which describes it as hardware, in limited availability, with ordering left to the Account team {{gap:pse-hardware-sales}}. The deployment guide gives a different Host Platform string for it {{divergence:appliance-host-platform}}.

prose.label: Not the ZIA product.
prose.text: {{separate-from-zia}} The ZIA inline inspection cluster is [[zia.private-service-edge.what-it-is]]. {{no-inspection}}
Where it sits in the tunnel path is in [[zpa.private-service-edges.data-path]]; whether to deploy one is in [[zpa.private-service-edges.when-to-deploy]].

checks.do: Which product the question is about, since ZPA and ZIA both have a Private Service Edge and they are different products.
Whether the question assumes the Private Service Edge inspects traffic, which a Private Access Service Edge does not.
Whether a user whose application is unreachable is being relayed through a Public Service Edge because no App Connector has a data connection to the Private Service Edge.
Whether a ZPA Appliance host platform appears on the Private Service Edge, to tell the appliance from a customer-built image.

single-tenant-broker.statement: A ZPA Private Service Edge is a single-tenant instance broker that provides the functionality of a Public Service Edge for Private Access in the organization's environment. The organization hosts it within its site or on a cloud service, and Zscaler manages it.

quotes: single-tenant instance brokers that provide the functionality of a Public Service Edge for Private Access
Your organization hosts them either within your site or on a cloud service, but Zscaler manages them.

broker-function.statement: Like a Public Service Edge, a Private Service Edge manages the connections between Zscaler Client Connector and App Connectors. It registers with the Private Access Cloud, which lets it download the relevant policies and configurations and enforce all Private Access policies, and it caches path selection decisions.

quotes: As with a Public Service Edge, a Private Service Edge manages the connections between Zscaler Client Connector and App Connectors. It registers with the Private Access Cloud.
This allows a Private Service Edge to download the relevant policies and configurations so it can enforce all Private Access policies. It also caches path selection decisions.

no-inspection.statement: In Private Access the Service Edge does not inspect the data as traffic flows through it, unlike a Service Edge in Internet & SaaS.

quotes: In Private Access, the Service Edge does not inspect the data as traffic flows through it.
In Internet & SaaS, the Service Edge inspects the data as traffic flows through it.

separate-from-zia.statement: Both Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Access have Service Edges, and Private Access runs on a multi-tenant infrastructure separate from that of Internet & SaaS.

quotes: Both Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Access have Service Edges.
Private Access runs on a unique multi-tenant infrastructure, separate from that of Internet & SaaS

upstream-public-se.statement: Each deployed Private Service Edge connects to a Public Service Edge, and the console shows which one. The name that Private Service Edges resolve to locate Public Service Edges is pb2br.

quotes: The Public Service Edge that the Private Service Edge connects to.
The endpoint for Private Service Edges to locate Public Service Edges is pb2br.

relay-via-public.statement: When the Private Service Edge has no direct connection to the App Connector serving an application, or no App Connector can establish a data connection to the Private Service Edge where the user is connected, the Private Service Edge forwards the request to a Public Service Edge (the nearest one, in the no-direct-connection case). The Public Service Edge connects to the closest App Connector it can reach and completes the request through the Private Service Edge with an additional hop.

quotes: If the Private Service Edge does not have a direct connection to the App Connector that is providing access to the application, the Private Service Edge forwards traffic to the nearest Public Service Edge for Private Access.

If no App Connector for the requested application can establish a data connection to the required Private Service Edge where the user is connected, then the Private Service Edge relays the Zscaler Client Connector request to a Public Service Edge.

The Public Service Edge then connects to the closest App Connector that it can reach for that application request and completes the application request via the Private Service Edge through an additional hop.

coexists-with-public.statement: A tenant's Private Service Edge groups sit alongside Public Service Edges: a group can be configured to be prioritized over a closer Public Service Edge.

quotes: to be prioritized over a closer Public Service Edge for Private Access.

coexists-with-public.conditions: Inferred: a per-group override that compares against Public Service Edges presupposes that both exist in one tenant.

zpa-appliance.statement: A ZPA Appliance is a Private Service Edge host platform: the console shows "ZT-8010-Zscaler Red Hat Image" as the host platform for one.

quotes: Private Service Edge Host Platform: The platform that the Private Service Edge is deployed on (e.g., AWS). If you are using a ZPA Appliance, ZT-8010-Zscaler Red Hat Image appears in this field.

pse-hardware-sales.title: Whether the ZPA Appliance is sold as dedicated hardware
pse-hardware-sales.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "It is not confirmed whether ZPA PSEs are virtual-only or also available as dedicated hardware. The help sources describe only VM images." The console field names a ZPA Appliance image ({{zpa-appliance}}), which shows an appliance exists.
pse-hardware-sales.resolution: The Understanding ZPA Appliances page says high-performance and high-throughput hardware appliances are available for Private Access App Connectors and Private Service Edges, with model, throughput and port specifications; it carries a limited-availability note (contact the Zscaler Account team). Still open: how it is ordered and what the limited-availability note covers. See zpa.software-components.appliance.
pse-hardware-sales.blocks: telling a customer whether a Private Service Edge can be bought as a physical appliance

appliance-host-platform.summary: The Host Platform string of a ZPA appliance Private Service Edge

quotes: If you are using a ZPA Appliance, ZT-8010-Zscaler Red Hat Image appears in this field.

positions.says: The About Private Service Edges page says ZT-8010-Zscaler Red Hat Image appears in the Host Platform field for a ZPA Appliance.

quotes: Click the Private Service Edge name and verify that the Host Platform is ZS-ZPA-PSE-8010.

positions.says: The appliance deployment page says to verify that the Private Service Edge's Host Platform is ZS-ZPA-PSE-8010.

appliance-host-platform.impact: The two pages give different strings for the Host Platform field of a ZPA appliance Private Service Edge.
